messages:
maya: Quick design check — uploading the latest mock for the Usage page. Main callout: do we prefer a transaction-ledger layout (row-per-action, inline token denom) or a rollup view (grouped by project/day with expandable details)? figma: https://figma.com/s/xyz

sam: love the ledger for debugging, but worried about scan density for org-level views. rollups would compress the timeline for large orgs.

liam: from an implementation POV ledger = more DOM rows, but we can virtualize. rollup + expand is trickier for keyboard nav.

maya: good point — accessibility is top of mind. For rollups, I think we need clear aria-expanded states and a persistent scope pill so users know which org/project they're viewing.

anya: copy nudge — instead of "Token breakdown" callout, can we try "Usage detail"? Less jargon for new accounts.

jordan: analytics note — when aggregated by org the token-per-request distribution gets skewed. If we show median + p95 next to rollup that helps surfacing outliers.

sam: also decision: invoice download CTA — do we keep it in row (per-transaction) or only on the grouped header (monthly invoice)? legal wants clear provenance per invoice.

maya: proposed pattern: default to rollup on org scope, default to ledger on project scope. Add a toggle at top: "List view" / "Grouped view" and store preference per-account. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

liam: storing preference per-account is straightforward. For keyboard users the toggle should be reachable with a single Tab stop.

anya: accessibility nit: ensure the toggle has aria-pressed and a descriptive label like `aria-label="View mode: list or grouped"`. Also add visible focus ring color that meets 4.5:1 contrast.

maya: copy for invoice CTA — draft: `Download invoice (CSV)` vs `Download statement (PDF)` — which is clearer?

sam: prefer `Download statement (PDF)` for billing teams, keep CSV as secondary for exports.

jordan: can we add a tiny sparkline next to each rollup row that shows token burn over the period? helpful for quick eyeballs.

liam: sparklines ok but render as SVGs with role="img" and aria-hidden if decorative. If conveying data, provide an offscreen accessible text: "Token trend: up 12%".

maya: UI micro-proposal pasted:
```
- Header: Scope pill (Org / Project)  •  Toggle: [List] [Grouped]
- Grouped row: Project name | total tokens | median latency | sparkline | Download statement (PDF)
- Expand detail: ledger rows with per-call token denom, timestamp, and invoice reference link
```

maya: also thinking about the token denomination display: show tokens + cost in fiat on hover or a persistent small inline chip?

anya: persistent inline chip is better for discoverability, hover-only loses keyboard and mobile users. Use abbreviated token label (e.g., "4.2k tokens • $0.23").

sam: mobile: probably default to grouped view with the ability to drill into a single project — ledger is too dense for phones.

jordan: when users switch scope from org -> project we should keep their view mode if they manually changed it during session. store in local session state + account preference.

liam: performance question: rollups require pre-aggregated endpoints. backend team needs an API flag `aggregate_by=project,day` — I'll sync with infra.

maya: question for design: where to surface invoice provenance? current mock puts a tiny invoice id inside each ledger row. Might be noisy. Alternative: include an "Invoice" column in the expanded ledger only.

anya: agree, keep the invoice id out of the compact group row — move to expanded detail and the per-invoice modal with full metadata (issued, due, line items).

sam: +1. Also add a secondary CTA in modal: "Export line items (CSV)" — finance loves that.

deploy-bot: new mock uploaded by maya at 2026-11-07T15:12:30Z — /figma/usage-v4

maya: next steps: I'll iterate on two mocks (org-grouped default + project-ledger default), add the aria changes, and surface copy variants for "Usage detail" vs "Token breakdown". I'll post follow-up with annotated diff.

liam: ping me when API flag is finalized, I'll wire up the toggle and sparklines.

anya: I'll run a quick a11y pass on the mock and test keyboard-only expand/collapse.

sam: timeline — can we get a prototype by Tues? that gives us runway to get legal sign-off on invoice wording.

maya: aiming for Monday EOD. thanks all :raised_hands:
